title: Scenario
description: Tool-agnostic definition of a single A/B test: one variable, two variants, exactly one primary KPI and at least one guardrail, plus the optional card layer scripts/build_card.py renders from the same file (one JSON per scenario). Deliberately independent of any testing platform's own schema; whoever imports it maps it to their tool. Several of CLAUDE.md's binding rules are enforced here structurally rather than in prose: rule 1 (three boxes, three to six items each), rule 2 (one primary KPI, listed first), rule 3 (a guardrail exists), rule 4 (one variable, two variants), rule 8 (source is stated, an adapted scenario names its archive original), rule 10 (evidence level is stated). Cross-field rules a schema cannot express (pre-registration agrees with the scenario, ring placement matches the difference type, numbers only with known traffic, the mockup markup allowlist) are checked by scripts/validate_scenario_json.py, which also prints warnings (a rate with no denominator, a lagging guardrail with no window, a guardrail that is the complement of the primary); --strict turns those into errors. A scenario is valid without a card object: the card layer is added when the scenario is rendered.

boxItem.description: One bullet in one of the three boxes. The object form carries a bold label; the string form is a plain line.

title.description: The scenario's question. Archive convention is an actual question ending in '?' — a title that asserts an answer prejudges the test.

stage.description: Journey stage / archive file this belongs to, e.g. cart-checkout

rationale.description: Why this is worth testing, in prose. Becomes the card's description.

lang.description: Rule 7: the language of the scenario text and of the card frame (box headers, role pills, footer labels, <html lang>). Defaults to tr when absent, for backward compatibility.

source.description: Rule 8: 'archive' = an archive scenario used as written; 'adapted' = an archive pattern fitted to this page (name it in adapted_from); 'generated' = produced for this page. Rendered as the card's source tag.

adapted_from.description: Rule 8: the title of the archive scenario an 'adapted' scenario comes from. Required when source is 'adapted' (checked by the validator).

objection.description: The objection the change answers (methodology.md: Trust, Price, Fit, Timing, Effort, Clarity), in the scenario's language. Rendered as a footer tag.

ice.description: ICE prioritisation (methodology.md → Prioritization). tier is the coarse band shown on the card; the three scores are optional, and when all three are given the tier must match their product (High ≥ 300, Medium 125-299, Low < 125).

variable.description: Rule 4: the ONE thing that differs between the variants. A value naming two things ('renk ve metin') is a rule-4 violation the schema cannot catch — scenario-critic does.

hypothesis.description: A hypothesis states a mechanism, not just a prediction. 'B will convert better' is a guess; 'B converts better because the coupon field stops sending code-less users off-site' is testable.

mechanism.description: The causal clause: why the change should move the metric.

device.description: The context the scenario lives in and the frame the card draws: phone = native app screen (tab bar only via card.bottom_nav), phone-web = page in a mobile browser (status bar + address bar, no tab bar), web = desktop browser. card.device overrides it for rendering. The former 'both' is gone: a card draws one frame, and the audience belongs in the setup spec.

market.description: Rule 11: market is separate from language. null means unknown — which is honest, and blocks carrying one market's result to another.

variants.description: Exactly two. A third variant is a different test design and this schema deliberately refuses to express it.

is_current.description: Rule 15: when the user shared a real page, variant A is that page as-is. Mark it true rather than quietly redesigning the control.

test_items.description: Rule 1: the 'What to test' box. Three to six items.

dont_items.description: Rule 1: the 'Never do' box. Three to six items.

kpis.description: Rule 1, 2 and 3, enforced structurally: three to six items, exactly one primary and it comes first, at least one guardrail; each metric is listed once. Rendered as the KPI box: name as the bold label, question as the text, role as a pill. Every line carries its denominator, in the name ("… (per assigned user)", "… (… başına)") or in the denominator field; a count ("Sayısı") or a "users who saw it" denominator is an error on the primary and a warning elsewhere.

denominator.description: What the metric is divided by, when the name does not say it (e.g. 'assigned users', 'users who reached the payment step, logged in both arms').

evidence.description: Rule 10: the strength of the evidence behind the proposal is always stated. A weak level is allowed; hiding it is not.

sample.description: Rule 5: no duration or sample promise without known traffic. Leave the numeric fields out rather than estimating them.

mde.description: Relative minimum detectable effect as a fraction (0.05 = 5%).

history.description: Rule 16: what .abtest-history.md says about this variable on this page.

preregistration.description: Optional. Decisions fixed before launch (ab-test-design's pre-registration block). The normal path is to validate it inside the scenario's own JSON (validate_scenario_json.py <scenario.json>), where its variable, primary KPI and guardrail names are checked against the scenario's: every guardrail of the KPI box is pre-registered and nothing else is. A bare {"preregistration": {...}} can be validated with --prereg-only as the fallback when no scenario JSON exists. The fields map onto the experiment-configuration fields common experimentation platforms ask for. Unknown numbers are null, never guessed (rule 5): planned_n_per_arm and duration_days may only be numbers when sample.traffic_known is true.

read_after_days.description: Follow-up window of a lagging primary (e.g. 'requests within 7 days of first open'): read only once that many days have passed for the last exposed cohort.

guardrails.description: Rule 3 with numbers. A guardrail is either margin-based (a tolerated relative degradation, read as one-sided non-inferiority) or a pass/fail check (type 'check' with a criterion saying what passing means, e.g. an accessibility review; no margin), never both. read_after_days marks a lagging guardrail (returns, 30-day refunds) that is read only once that many days have passed after exposure; the decision rule then says nothing ships before that window closes.

criterion.description: What passing means, e.g. 'keyboard and screen-reader review finds no critical issue'.

mde.description: Relative minimum detectable effect as a fraction (0.05 = 5%), or null when unknown.

alternative.description: 'greater' only with primary_kpi.direction 'increase', 'less' only with 'decrease' (checked by the validator).

allocation.description: Share of traffic per arm; the keys are the variant ids (A and B) and the shares sum to 1 (checked by the validator). A third arm is a different design: one pre-registration block per comparison.

trigger.description: The trigger event of a triggered analysis (methodology.md → KPI denominator), logged at the same point in both arms, before the change is shown. Absent = the assigned population.

pre_start_gates.description: What must be closed before the test takes traffic: compliance sign-off on B's exact copy in a regulated flow, a pass/fail guardrail checked on B, a lagging window still to be verified from product terms.

segments.description: Segments declared before launch — the only ones read as more than exploratory.

card.description: Optional visual layer consumed by scripts/build_card.py: the same JSON renders the card. Absent when the scenario is only being designed, reviewed or exported; added at render time.

variant_a.description: Mockup body of the control, raw markup built from the template's .r-* components. Only the allowlisted inert tags and attributes pass (build_card.py: ALLOWED_TAGS / ALLOWED_ATTRS, every attribute value in double quotes, no comments, links, images, forms or scripts); anything else is refused, not cleaned.

variant_b.description: Mockup body of the test variant; differs from variant_a in exactly one element.

difference.description: How B differs from A (the archive's 'Fark:' line). Enforces ring placement: add → .hl only in B; remove → .hl only in A plus shift_note_b; move → .hl in both; change → .hl in B (A optional). A change applied to N repeated elements gets ONE ring around the group.

device.description: Frame override; defaults to the scenario's device, then phone.

url.description: Address bar text (web) or the domain shown in the mobile address bar (phone-web). Required for those two frames.

bottom_nav.description: phone only: the real app's tab labels, a list of strings. Absent or empty = no tab bar (never invent one). Refused on phone-web and web, which draw no tab bar.

bottom_nav_active.description: The tab the screen belongs to, as that tab's label or its 0-based index in bottom_nav; drawn in the brand colour. The same tab is active in A and B. Ignored without bottom_nav.

brand.description: Rule 12: brand colours taken from the shared screen or a brand guide. Absent = neutral palette. A colour is #hex, rgb()/hsl() or a CSS colour name; any other word is refused by the validator and the builder (it would render a transparent button).

brand_note.description: Rule 12's one-line note under the card. Absent = a default (screen colours when brand is set, neutral palette otherwise); null or empty = no note (an official guide is in use).

mockup_basis.description: What the mockup is drawn from. described → footer says it was rebuilt from the user's description; representative → footer says it is a representative example. Absent = shared_page when a variant is_current, representative otherwise.

note_pos.description: Default position of every ring label; a single ring can override with data-pos.

shift_note_b.description: One line under mockup B; required for difference 'remove' (the content below moved up).

footer_notes.description: Notes about the drawing only (what wasn't visible, masked or left out); never advice. One exception: a line starting 'Stronger alternative:' / 'Daha güçlü alternatif:' on a weak test the user explicitly asked for.
